capabilities.scope: Rigid articulated URDF/SRDF import, semantic names, meshes, and deterministic fingerprints.
No production MJCF parser. A pinned G1 companion-MJCF preset is data, not general MJCF support.

Qualified Apple-Metal rigid, articulated, and rod solver path: fixed temporal microsteps, coupled nonlinear block sweeps, retained banded rod response for generalized and surface-contact rows, immediate integration, and transactional warm state. This does not qualify all rod mechanics or the residual-converged profile.
Private residual-converged NumiSolver profile is available for focused study; its current backend is transitional and not yet the qualified production path.
NumiSolver uses temporal small steps but does not claim the complete vendor-specific PhysX TGS contract.
Shared row, endpoint, cone, stable-key, and warm-start representation. Active scalar joint limits and contacts are coupled in NumiSolver; generic runtime widths beyond three rows remain incomplete.
Selected convex event-time paths exist; complete advance-to-impact, solve, and continue coverage is not qualified.
Distinct fingerprinted URDF, companion-MJCF, and RL Lab actuator contracts; no silent 25/35/50 N m mixing.

Swift schedules bounded native submissions; Metal owns persistent simulator state, asynchronous tickets, and per-environment physical publication. Whole-session atomic reset across TaskIR, actuators, tactile, presentation, and future recurrent policy state remains incomplete.

A reset is applied to working state only. A later pair-capacity failure restores the exact previously committed q/v, scene bodies, manifold headers/points/counts, SensorIR output and metadata, retains the resident token, and permits a following submission. Generalized warm starts, rods, and convex caches use the same pre-reset checkpoint ordering in code but still need focused reset-failure evidence.

The generated runtime schema owns every reachable pipeline, feature group, Metal entry point, host member, and threadgroup contract. Compiled feature selection creates only the required groups, later upgrades are additive, and three mutable state arenas share one immutable device/library/queue/pipeline cache. Metal 4 command allocators, generated argument tables, residency sets, and the final barrier graph remain incomplete.

In-process Swift/MLX PPO consumes lifetime-scoped native shared Metal rollout slots without Swift array concatenation, a Swift-side stream copy, an MLX input copy, duplicate compact MetalWorldResult vectors, or a CPU payload scan. The integration owner advances beyond the three-slot ring and validates release, policy revision, checkpoints, and artifacts.

The native runtime owns three fixed-capacity shared Metal slots for actor and critic observations, latents, behavior metadata, values, bootstrap values, and transitions. Swift receives only opaque leases; managed MLX C arrays retain and release the slot payload deterministically.

The world command buffer blits every compact learning stream directly into the pending native rollout lease. The lease cursor advances only with accepted world publication; the owner checks two-chunk offsets, bootstrap placement, byte-exact content, premature visibility rejection, exclusivity, reuse, and a leased-only result with zero duplicate host learning elements.

One cooperative Metal threadgroup validates every compact float and transition, then emits a 64-byte generated-ABI status containing failure attribution, checked counts, runtime ABI, policy revision, task fingerprint, and a unique submission token. The CPU reads only this status before advancing a lease.
Fixed- and floating-base tasks share compiled semantic bindings, native joint/contact observations, reward, termination, reset, curriculum, and randomization.

Compiled frames can target links in any articulation or static, kinematic, and dynamic scene bodies. Explicit frame-to-frame operators publish reference-local position and tangent orientation across domains without overloading static goals. World and moving-reference linear/angular velocity operators are materialized from accepted generalized and scene state once per control step, including the rotating-frame transport term; the same path supplies physically consistent support-slip and clearance metrics. Static SE(3) goals, pose rewards and terminations, SensorIR scalar/validity sources, and reset-correct pre-policy state are implemented. Site semantics, acceleration, point/Jacobian quantities, sampled or trajectory goals, generic reductions, and three complete task families are not yet qualified.

TaskIR resolves named SensorIR scalar values and validity bits, including fresh-but-invalid coherent dropout, enforces actor/critic permissions, fingerprints the exact sensor program, seeds histories transactionally on reset, advances them from accepted post-physics state, and republishes terminal policy/value views before inference.

Every native task step journals per-environment task state, action delay, and compact contact metrics; reset steps additionally journal actor/critic/clean histories, previous velocity, sensor bias, and body/controller randomization. A rejected reset keeps its typed failure transition but restores hidden state, and the next accepted physics, task, policy, sensor, and contact outputs match a no-failure reference branch byte-for-byte. Global curriculum scheduling is not included.
Native deformation, contact evidence, wrench summaries, history, and device-buffer access.

Native parent-frame pose, world-space frame-twist, six-axis IMU, six-axis contact-wrench, and five-channel contact-state sensors use topology-derived persistent buffers, reset-only seeding, accepted-state advancement, deterministic nanosecond phase accumulation, whole-sample latency history, and compact value/age/validity publication. Twist linear velocity is evaluated at the authored sensor origin. Force-torque and contact-state consume final-microstep NumiSolver impulses; semantic contact filters are immutable compiled tables. The owner covers articulated and rigid kinematic parents, exact 50 Hz and non-divisor 30 Hz schedules, reset-cleared contact signals, and task-independent execution.

A generic body-attached IMU publishes sensor-local specific force followed by sensor-local angular velocity. Specific force differentiates accepted sensor-origin world velocity over the exact scheduled interval and subtracts world gravity; previous point velocity and timestamp are persistent transactionally journaled SensorIR state. The owner checks a rotated kinematic parent against an analytic acceleration/gravity/gyro result and includes IMU state in rejected-reset branch equivalence.

Only environments requesting reset journal their SensorIR schedule state, corruption episode identity, complete latency ring, compact output, and metadata in private topology-sized buffers. A rejected world or contact transaction restores the journal byte-for-byte, keeps the resident token valid, and permits a following submission; successful and ordinary non-reset steps perform no checkpoint copy.

Six-axis SensorIR force-torque sums committed non-generalized contact impulses on the parent body, divides by the final accepted physics-microstep duration, shifts the moment to the authored sensor origin, and expresses force and torque in sensor-local axes. All six channels match TaskIR's independent contact-group reduction and reset clears the view. Control-window integration and joint-transmission load-cell semantics remain incomplete.

A generic body-attached contact-state sensor publishes active state, accepted contact-block count, summed normal force, resultant tangential force, and maximum penetration from committed NumiSolver constraints. Optional semantic counterpart-body filters compile into a canonical immutable index table. The focused owner mirrors all five reductions analytically, proves a negative filter remains zero, rejects an unresolved filter transactionally, round-trips the semantic filter through WorldPack, binds the result into TaskIR, and includes its state in reset rollback.

Native scalar SensorIR publication applies episode-static Gaussian bias, per-acquired-sample Gaussian value noise, and coherent whole-sensor dropout from a stateless counter key containing session seed, environment, episode, stable sensor ID, sample, channel, and purpose. Pose orientation noise is a normalized tangent-space rotation; contact-state discrete channels remain exact. The owner checks host-mirrored twist and pose values, exact replay, seed separation, episode reset, explicit dropped validity through TaskIR, WorldPack persistence, and rejected-reset rollback. Presentation and tactile corruption remain in their current native owners until schedule unification.

WorldPack state, frame-twist, IMU, force-torque, contact-state, image, and tactile declarations compile transactionally into one generated-ABI descriptor table. State-pose, frame-twist, IMU, force-torque, and semantically filtered contact-state sensors execute in the session-owned scheduler with reset-failure journals, native counter-based corruption, and TaskIR bindings; presentation and tactile still use their existing native owners, while recorder routing, ray, and LiDAR operators remain incomplete.

Fingerprint-bound normalization, dense actor/critic layers, Gaussian behavior policy, and native inference. Each dense output is reduced cooperatively in FP32 by one SIMDgroup, up to eight outputs share a threadgroup, and the owner compares nonzero rollout outputs with a host dot-product reference. SIMDgroup matrix tiles and reduced-precision storage remain unqualified.

A stable topology fingerprint locks the compiled policy shape. Changed parameters require a monotonic revision, upload into the inactive one of two private Metal banks, and become active only at a native submission boundary. The task owner proves A-to-B-to-A reuse; the Swift integration rejects stale and topology-changing updates transactionally. Direct no-copy MLX-to-bank blits remain incomplete.
Convolution, recurrence, and attention are not production PolicyIR operators.
Forward Jacobians exist, but no production tape, backward kernels, implicit adjoint, or validity-mask API exists.
Authored Visual Presentation V3 path; collision geometry is not a visual fallback.
